Re-Verify an Entire Reproducible Data Capsule

Source: R/lib_capsule.R
vrfcps.Rd

Runs the full custody chain over a capsule directory in one call and reports, check by check, whether the capsule is still the one the analysis was run on: the provenance record is readable, the pinned data file is present and has its recorded SHA-256, the schema still validates, a recorded analysis script still has its pinned hash, every numeric cross-check in a results manifest still reproduces its recorded verdict, and the data are real rather than synthetic. Use it before re-running or publishing an analysis, or when receiving a capsule from someone else.

Usage

vrfcps(
  cpsdir,
  provfile = "data_provenance.json",
  dfile = NULL,
  mnffile = NULL,
  scrfile = NULL
)

Arguments

cpsdir

Directory containing the capsule, a single string.

provfile

Provenance JSON filename, relative to cpsdir. "data_provenance.json" is the default.

dfile

Data filename relative to cpsdir. NULL (the default) uses the provenance's resource$filename.

mnffile

Optional results-manifest JSON (as written by wrmnfjs()), relative to cpsdir. NULL (the default) uses manifest.json when the capsule has one.

scrfile

Optional analysis-script filename relative to cpsdir; compared against the pinned script digest. NULL (the default) uses the script named in the provenance or the manifest, if any.

Value

An object of class c("bricklayer_capsule_check", "list"), printed as one line per check:

ok

logical scalar, the overall verdict described in Details.

checks

data.frame with columns check (character, the check name), ok (logical) and detail (character: the path checked, the digest found, or why it failed).

required

character, the checks that had to be made.

missing

character, required checks that were never made (character(0) when none).

Details

The checks, in the order they appear in checks:

provenance_readable

provfile is a plain relative path inside the capsule (no .., no absolute path, no symlink out) and parses as JSON.

data_present

the data file (dfile, else the provenance's resource$filename) is inside the capsule and is a file.

data_sha256

vrfsha256() finds that its SHA-256 equals resource$sha256 (64 hex characters).

data_size_bytes

when resource$size_bytes is recorded: the size on disk matches.

data_readable

a .csv file is read with utils::read.csv(); a non-CSV file fails this row when a row count or schema is recorded (they cannot be checked).

data_row_count

when resource$row_count_data_rows is recorded: the CSV has that many rows.

schema_valid

when a schema is recorded: valsch() finds no fatal issue (warnings are listed in detail but pass).

manifest_consistent

when mnffile is given, or the capsule holds manifest.json: every result with numeric observed and expected, a tol and a status of PASS or DIFFER still gets that status from \(|observed - expected| \le tol\).

script_sha256

when a script is named (by scrfile, by script$filename in the provenance or by meta$scrfile in the manifest) or a script digest is pinned (meta$script_sha256 or script$sha256): the script's SHA-256 matches the pin.

data_not_synthetic

no <data>.synthetic sidecar (written by mksyncsv()), and neither the manifest nor the provenance records synthetic = true.

A check that cannot be made because the provenance lacks a field is a FAILED row, never skipped: a provenance of {} verifies nothing. ok is TRUE only when every row passed and every required check was made. The required checks are provenance_readable, data_present, data_sha256 and data_not_synthetic, plus manifest_consistent and script_sha256 when a manifest or a script is in play.

Entirely offline: nothing is downloaded and nothing is written. Error: cpsdir that is not one existing directory. Every other problem is a failed row, not an error.

Examples

dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "capsule-example")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(id = 1:3), file.path(dir, "d.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
prov <- list(resource = list(filename = "d.csv",
                             sha256 = sha256file(file.path(dir, "d.csv")),
                             row_count_data_rows = 3),
             schema = list(expected_columns = "id"))
writeLines(tojs(prov, auto_unbox = TRUE),
           file.path(dir, "data_provenance.json"))
vrfcps(dir)$ok
#> [1] TRUE
vrfcps(dir)
#> Capsule verification: intact (7 of 7 checks passed)
#>   ok    provenance_readable  /tmp/Rtmp5LSEh0/capsule-example/data_provenance.json
#>   ok    data_present         /tmp/Rtmp5LSEh0/capsule-example/d.csv
#>   ok    data_sha256          da4aaa3a009d063f36d0515f2b50a11bcc578264aa7c45504b46fedbbae4f8f7
#>   ok    data_readable        /tmp/Rtmp5LSEh0/capsule-example/d.csv
#>   ok    data_row_count       3 rows on disk
#>   ok    schema_valid         
#>   ok    data_not_synthetic   no synthetic marker: sidecar, manifest and provenance all say real data

# an edited data file fails its digest and its row count
write.csv(data.frame(id = 1:4), file.path(dir, "d.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
chk <- vrfcps(dir)
chk$ok
#> [1] FALSE
chk$checks[!chk$checks$ok, c("check", "detail")]
#>            check
#> 3    data_sha256
#> 5 data_row_count
#>                                                                                                                                            detail
#> 3 expected da4aaa3a009d063f36d0515f2b50a11bcc578264aa7c45504b46fedbbae4f8f7, got b24bb2c082053f4d1f5db97140babb86d4cc7e31b49be4e3c4cf94ca87a86d2b
#> 5                                                                                                                                  4 rows on disk

# a path out of the capsule is a failed check, not a read
vrfcps(dir, provfile = "../elsewhere.json")$ok
#> [1] FALSE

# a missing directory is an error
try(vrfcps(file.path(tempdir(), "no-such-capsule")))
#> Error : `cpsdir` is not an existing directory: /tmp/Rtmp5LSEh0/no-such-capsule
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
